payload.title: Derive test regression by diffing runs against the last-green baseline
payload.description: Split out of E-1771. Determine whether a failing test is a regression (passed on a prior commit, now broken) versus never-worked — computed by diffing a run against the last-green baseline in captured test history, NOT asserted by the agent (a single session lacks a trustworthy baseline; asking it to classify invites 'probably not my fault' self-cover). Frame the result as a recoverability signal — 'this test has a known-green ancestor, so a working version exists in VCS' — not blame; most meaningful at project scope. Blocked by E-1777: regression can only be derived once test-run history is captured as structured rows.

# `endless task report <id> --xml=<…>` — structured handoff/report command

Full design rationale: see E-1760 outcome. **Element set grounded by E-1774**
(28-session handoff analysis) — read that outcome for the concern taxonomy and
the reasoning behind every partition below.

## Core idea
Make ceremony **unrepresentable** rather than detectable. The agent's
end-of-session report stops being freeform prose it composes and becomes the
verbatim output of a command it feeds a structured XML payload. There is no
"State outside endless: none" because there is no field to put it in.

This is the durable enforcement layer sitting after E-1758 (handoff-status,
the git-anomaly computation) and E-1759 (spawn-prompt exception rule). The
worked example in E-1760's analysis is the reference specimen — including the
Turn 3 "inventory of the silence" meta-ceremony that a phrase deny-list cannot
catch. Phrase matching is explicitly rejected (too many FP/FN); determinism
comes from removing the freeform surface, not from matching prose better.

## Schema (grounded by E-1774)

E-1774's headline finding: once nothing computable is asked of the agent, the
**"validated-value" middle bucket collapses to empty** — every constrained field
(test result, external state, git facts) is computable or
computable-given-capture. The schema is therefore **computed on one side, gated
free-text on the other, with no editorializing middle.**

### Agent-supplied `--xml` payload — gated free text ONLY
```xml
<report>
  <note kind="anomaly|discovery">MEMORY files edited outside the branch won't land</note>
  <question>Develop go-cambria in a go-pkgs worktree, or directly in the repo?</question>
</report>
```
- `<note>` — repeats; attribute `kind`. The one escape hatch, guarded by the
  per-entry Haiku check (Requirement 4). Real specimens from the sample: "MEMORY
  files edited outside the branch won't land"; "base is behind main"; "E-1648
  landed mid-session"; a rebase-conflict-resolution narrative.
- `<question>` — repeats. Genuine "done, but I need your call on X." Not
  ceremony, so it gets a **different** per-entry check ("a real decision you
  need, or restating settled state?"), not the anomaly check. Reconcile the
  keyword interaction with E-1773's mid-session `FULL STATUS` bypass.
- The normal path is an empty `<report/>` — the command computes and renders
  everything else. Zero free-text entries ⇒ zero Haiku calls.

### Computed by the command and rendered (agent types none of it)
- **git/worktree anomalies** — `monitor.WorktreeAnomalies` (E-1758); empty ⇒
  silence.
- **verify command**, **follow-ups spawned** (link query), **deliverable
  pointer**, **this-task status**, **epic children**, **commit state** —
  computed from existing data and rendered into the relay output.

### Split to follow-ups — NOT this task
- **Structured capture of the report into queryable DB rows → E-1777**
  (brainstorm). E-1771 renders from existing/computed data; it does not build a
  `session_reports` persistence layer.
- **Test-result element (`<tests>` from CTRF) → rides with the capture work
  (E-1777)**; E-1771's first cut does not surface test results.
- **Regression-diffing (worked-then-broke, a VCS-recoverability signal) →
  E-1778** (blocked_by E-1777 — needs captured history to diff against).

### Removed / given NO element (this is the point)
- **Return line** — legacy (`spawner_task` / `return_anchor` decouple). Gone
  from the relay output.
- **External state** — no element. E-1774's search of ~60 sessions found it is
  *pure ceremony* ("no external/CI state"), zero real positives; the rare real
  case rides `<note kind="discovery">`. **Also strike the "flag external state"
  line from the handoff templates** — it manufactures the negative.
- Clean-state confirmations, landed-vs-worktree delta, status recap,
  gitignored-artifact notes, "what changed" prose, self-correction.

## Requirements
1. **Gated free-text payload, not a validated value-set.** Per E-1774 there are
   no validated-value fields — the payload carries only `<note>` and
   `<question>` free-text entries. Rejection is verb-check-style
   (`click.ClickException`, non-zero, anti-rationalization phrasing) but applies
   to a bounced **entry** via the Haiku gate, not to an out-of-set enum value.
   The agent supplies genuinely non-computable facts and open decisions; nothing
   else.
2. **Computes what the tool can compute.** The command calls handoff-status
   (E-1758) for git/worktree facts and resolves commit state, follow-ups,
   status, and epic children. The agent never types these, so it can never dress
   "working tree clean" — it was never asked. (Persisting these facts as
   queryable DB rows, and test-result ingestion, are E-1777 — not this task.)
3. **Self-complete relay output.** The command returns the *entire* final
   message — anomalies (or nothing) + how-to-verify, fully formed. The agent's
   job is "print this, add nothing before or after." This kills the envelope
   leak ("Here's my handoff! 🎉 …").
4. **Per-entry check (Haiku), scoped.** Each free-text entry gets a per-entry
   classifier — anomaly entries: "a real thing the reviewer could not compute,
   or the absence of a problem?"; question entries: "a real decision needed, or
   restating settled state?". It bounces the *entry*, not the message, and fires
   **only when a free-text entry is present** (empty `<report/>` ⇒ zero calls).
   **Haiku is sufficient and fixed** — a bounded per-entry classification, not
   the freeform-paragraph case the schema eliminates by construction. Pick the
   model that works (Haiku) and keep it; it is NOT a config knob (a value that
   works generally has no reason to vary). Swapping the LLM *provider* entirely
   (Codex, Llama, …) may matter someday but is a separate, large feature —
   explicitly out of scope here.
5. **Tunable check wording (user lever).** The check prompt(s) live in a
   user-editable config surface (verbs.jsonl-style precedent), NOT hardcoded in
   the product template. When the user catches the agent freelancing, the user
   tells the agent to improve the wording and the agent edits the *config*, not
   the product. Handoff-message templates may become tunable the same way later;
   start with the check wording. (The model itself is fixed, not tunable — Req 4.)

## Naming
Verb `report`, one positional (`<id>`), payload via `--xml`. Chosen over
`handoff` because this command is the vehicle for *all* end-of-session
reporting, not only the final handoff.

## Status-agnostic
The command is not tied to one status. It is the reporting vehicle at whatever
terminal status the agent reaches (unverified / assumed / completed --outcome).

payload.title: Replace less with a pannable terminal viewer so wide tables stay readable
payload.description: E-1775 makes markdown tables always fit the screen width and rely on vertical scroll, because less -R wraps any over-width line into an unreadable mess (it only pans on manual arrow-chop, and launching with -S would also chop the soft-wrapped prose). That is a stopgap: a genuinely wide table gets squeezed into narrow, tall columns with no way to see the full-width layout. The long-term fix is to replace the external less pager (spawned from task_cmd for -p) with a self-contained terminal viewer supporting smooth horizontal panning plus vertical scroll, so a table can render at natural width and the user pans left-right (columns sliding, not replaced). Mike's go-tealeaves teagrid (a BubbleTea grid pager) is prior art and a likely basis; this also drops the external less dependency (the E-1746 deferred note). Scope to settle when planned: general pager vs table-aware grid, less fallback, pan interaction model.

payload.title: Document the session navigation and status commands in the sessions guide
payload.description: docs/guide/sessions.md covers status snapshots, discovery (who am I), and reading cross-session state, but not the navigation/status command family that has since grown: goto, back, trail, monitor, activity, order, history, search, cd, use, forget, hide/unhide, recap. Each of these carries the generic agent_help pointer '▸ AGENT — read this before using this command: endless guide sessions' (from the guide-map), so the pointer resolves to a section that never explains them. Add coverage so the cross-reference is honest. Note these navigation commands (goto/back/monitor) are user-facing, not agent-directed. Scope: sessions guide only — the broader guide-map coverage gaps (agents/epic/verify/note/phrase/setup/docs) are out of scope here.

# E-1308 — Detect already-landed situations in `worktree land` and message accordingly

## Context

`endless worktree land E-NNN` mishandles three "the work already landed" situations
by treating them as failures:

- The worktree was removed by a prior land → `_branch_for_task` returns `None` and
  land raises `"No endless-managed worktree for E-NNN"` (`worktree_cmd.py:1628-1632`),
  implying the work is lost. It isn't — it's in main.
- The branch was rewritten relative to a landing that already happened (e.g. a
  `git commit --amend` of an already-landed commit) → land proceeds straight into a
  confusing Step-4 rebase conflict. Observed repro: the E-1750 land amended a
  landed commit; the re-land conflicted in `session_status.go`.

Full scope decided with Mike 2026-07-11: cover all three via one shared last-landing
lookup — A1 (branch merged), A2 (branch also reaped), B (branch is a rewrite).

## 1. New capability — read a task's last landing (Go)

No Go query returns a task's landing SHA today (`session-query` has none; the Python
`landed_item` path reads `task_landings` via SQLite, which new code must not extend —
E-1486). Add subcommand **`session-query last-landing --id <task-id>`** in
`internal/sessionquerycmd/session_query.go` (dispatched from the `session-query` case
in `cmd/endless-go/main.go`; update the usage lines at `main.go:14` and `:195`).

Query (main DB):

    SELECT merge_commit_sha, branch, landed_at
      FROM task_landings WHERE task_id = ?
     ORDER BY landed_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT 1

Output: JSON `{"merge_commit_sha","branch","landed_at"}`; empty output when the task
has no landing (mirror the empty-handling of the existing subcommands, e.g.
`task-text`). Python wraps it as `_last_landing(task_id) -> dict | None` via
`shutil.which("endless-go")` + `config.go_db_context_args()` (land already pins main
through `default_db_to_main`), returning `None` when there is no landing.

## 2. Facet A — worktree already gone (`land_worktree`, the `target is None` branch ~L1632)

Before raising "No endless-managed worktree", in order:

- **A1 (git-only):** a branch matching `task/<NNN>-*` exists AND is listed by
  `git branch --merged <base>` → print
  `"E-<NNN> already landed (<branch-tip-short-sha>); its worktree was removed by an
  earlier land. Nothing to do."` and RETURN success (exit 0).
- **A2 (uses §1):** else, if `_last_landing(NNN)` is not None → print
  `"E-<NNN> already landed (<merge_commit_sha-short>); its worktree and branch were
  reaped. Nothing to do."` and RETURN success.
- **A3:** else → today's `"No endless-managed worktree for E-<NNN>"` error (the work
  is genuinely unaccounted for).

The subject task's own `E-<NNN>` may appear (the user typed it); the house-rule ban is
on citing UNRELATED internal task IDs — none here.

## 3. Facet B — branch is a rewrite of already-landed content (pre-rebase gate)

Insert after Step 3.8's dirty guard (`_guard_dirty_worktree`, ~L1741) and BEFORE
Step 4's `git rebase base_branch` (~L1743):

- `land = _last_landing(NNN)`; if `None` → skip (first land — normal).
- Else if `git -C <wt> merge-base --is-ancestor <land.merge_commit_sha> HEAD` exits
  non-zero → HEAD is NOT a descendant of the landing → the branch was rewritten
  relative to it. **Refuse before the rebase mutates anything:**
  `raise click.ClickException(msg)` where `msg` states the branch was rewritten
  relative to its landing at `<sha>` and gives the definitive recovery — capture the
  new delta, `git reset --hard <base>`, re-apply only the delta, commit, retry —
  each git command on ONE physical line, no emojis, no unrelated internal IDs. Use
  wording identical to E-1417's reset+reapply candidate so the two surfaces read the
  same.
- Else (descendant, or no landing) → proceed to Step 4 unchanged.

A correct follow-up (a new commit on a branch first rebased onto main) passes,
because main contains the landing SHA; only an amend/rewrite of the landed commit is
refused. This makes the amend case a precise PRE-conflict refusal; E-1417 remains the
after-conflict safety net for source conflicts B cannot predetermine.

## Files
- `internal/sessionquerycmd/session_query.go` (+ usage lines in `cmd/endless-go/main.go`)
  — the `last-landing` subcommand.
- `src/endless/worktree_cmd.py` — `_last_landing` helper; Facet A block at the
  `target is None` branch; Facet B gate before Step 4.

## Coordination with E-1417 (in flight, same function)
E-1417 rewrites Step 4's conflict handler; E-1308 adds a pre-Step-4 gate and the
`target is None` branch — adjacent code. Rebase E-1308 onto E-1417 (or sequence after
it). Share the reset+reapply wording between B's message and E-1417's candidate. No
behavioral clash: B refuses earlier, so E-1417's Step-4 handler is simply not reached
for the rewrite case.

## Tests
- Go (`internal/sessionquerycmd`, pattern per its `*_test.go`): `last-landing` returns
  the newest landing's SHA; empty when none.
- Python worktree-land suite (real git repos, pattern per
  `tests/test_worktree_land_orphan_drop.py`):
  - A1: worktree dir removed + branch merged → friendly message, exit 0.
  - A2: worktree + branch gone + a `task_landings` row → friendly message.
  - A3: neither → today's error preserved.
  - B: landed once then branch amended (not a descendant) → refuse before rebase with
    reset+reapply; branch with a new commit stacked (descendant) → proceeds.

## Verify
Deliver `tests/tasks/e-1308-verify.sh`; handoff is exactly:

    esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1308-verify.sh

Exercises A1/A2/A3/B against crafted throwaway git repos plus the `last-landing` Go
query, per the model of `tests/tasks/e-1577-verify.sh`.

## Non-goals
- Auto-recovering the rewrite (Facet B refuses + instructs; it does not reset for the
  user — land stays non-interactive).
- Changing the reaper or the landing-record flow.
- Replacing E-1417's after-conflict diagnosis (kept as the safety net).

# E-1780 — Document the session navigation/status commands in the sessions guide

## Context

`docs/guide/sessions.md` covers status snapshots (`snapshot add`), "who am I"
discovery, and the DB internals of the status subsystem — but **none** of the
navigation / observation / inspection command family that has since grown on the
`session` group. Because `agent_help` prepends "▸ AGENT — read this before using this
command: `endless guide sessions`" to every `session` subcommand's `--help` (the
generic guide-map cross-reference), the pointer sends people to a section that never
explains `goto`, `back`, `monitor`, `activity`, and the rest.

This task makes the sessions guide honest about that pointer. It also clears the
confusion that started this: those `▸ AGENT` prefixes are a blanket per-command guide
pointer, not a claim that the commands are agent-only — `goto`/`back`/`monitor` are
user commands, and the guide will say so.

Confirmed while drafting (2026-07-14):
- `session snapshot` still exposes only `add`; the `latest`/`show`/`list` reads the
  guide calls "forthcoming" genuinely have not shipped — so that section stays
  forward-looking, only retitled (see Deliverable 2).
- `task verify` has shipped and top-level `verify` is gone, so the guide-map coverage
  gap E-1607 flagged is already closed — unrelated to this task, just noted.

## Approach

Additive and low-disruption: keep the existing snapshot content intact, add **one
broad section** with tight subsections (per the few-broad-sections principle — one new
`##`, not six), plus one retitle and one framing note. Match the existing terse,
complete house style.

## Deliverables

### 1. New section: `## Navigating & observing sessions`

Placed after "Discovery: who am I?" (both are about operating across sessions).
A short lead paragraph states the audience split: **navigation and the live view
(`goto`/`back`/`monitor`) are things the user drives from tmux; the inspection
commands are where an agent coordinating across sessions reaches.** Then subsections:

- **Navigating (`goto` / `back` / `trail`)** — `goto <task|session>` switches tmux
  focus to that pane (a task id resolves to its most-recently-active live session) and
  pushes the current pane onto a per-client back-stack; `back` pops it browser-style
  (empty stack → the spawning session); `trail` shows the durable from→to move log
  (with the `manual`/`goto` via-tag and relative time). All require tmux.
- **Watching live (`status` / `monitor`)** — `status` renders a one-shot view of the
  focal task plus its spawning task, sibling sessions, and cross-session in-flight
  work; `--tree` renders the do/plan backlog in implementation order. `monitor` is the
  top-like loop of that same view (redraws every 2s, Ctrl-C to exit) — the pane you
  keep open all day.
- **Inspecting a session (`show` / `list` / `activity` / `history` / `search` /
  `recap`)** — `list` recent sessions; `show` one session's detail; `activity`
  projects what a session did from the event ledger (Filed / Claimed / Shipped /
  Confirmed / …); `history` its conversation; `search` across all session messages;
  `recap` Claude-generated summaries.
- **Ordering & visibility (`order` / `hide` / `unhide`)** — `order` sets this
  session's per-task implementation order (a `|`-grouped SPEC; equal ranks =
  parallelizable) which drives `status --tree`; `hide`/`unhide` manage what appears in
  `session list`.

Density: a compact "one row/line per command" reference (see Open Decision 3), each
line a single sentence of what-it-does + the audience, not prose-per-command.

### 2. Retitle the snapshot-reading section

`## Reading status (forward-looking — E-1319)` now collides with the newly-documented
`session status`. Retitle to `## Reading snapshots` (its content is `session
snapshot` reads). Keep it forward-looking — those reads have not shipped — and drop
the bare `E-1319` from the heading per the no-task-ids-in-shipped-docs rule.

### 3. Shell-entry cross-reference (`use` / `cd` / `forget`)

One line, not a re-documentation: note that `session use` / `session cd` /
`session forget` are the shell-evaluable backends of the `esu` / `esp` / `esf` helpers,
and point at the **Shell helpers** section of `endless guide orchestration`.
(See Open Decision 1.)

### 4. Verification — `tests/tasks/e-1780-verify.sh`

Lightweight, modeled on `tests/tasks/e-1607-verify.sh`. Assert against the worktree's
own file (the global `endless guide` reads the main checkout's docs, not this branch):
- `docs/guide/sessions.md` documents each navigation/observation/inspection command
  name (`goto`, `back`, `trail`, `status`, `monitor`, `show`, `list`, `activity`,
  `history`, `search`, `recap`, `order`, `hide`, `unhide`);
- it carries the `use`/`cd`/`forget` → orchestration cross-reference;
- the "Navigating & observing sessions" heading exists and the audience-framing note
  is present;
- the guide still renders (no new top-level slug; `endless guide --list` unchanged).

## Open decisions (for your steer before I finalize)

1. **`use`/`cd`/`forget`** — cross-reference to the orchestration shell-helpers section
   (recommended), or document them in full here too?
2. **Pre-existing `E-NNNN` citations** — `sessions.md` is full of them (E-1688, E-1319,
   E-1284, E-1683, E-1318, E-1315, E-1208, …), which breaks the
   no-task-ids-in-shipped-docs rule. Recommendation: inline/strip only the ones in
   sections this task touches; leave the rest for a separate hygiene task. Or fold the
   whole-file pass in here?
3. **Density** — a table-driven "one row per command" reference (recommended, terse),
   or prose-per-command with a usage example each?

## Verification (handoff to Mike)

Set `unverified`; run `esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1780-verify.sh`.

fields.analysis:
Scope decision (with Mike, 2026-07-11): FULL — A1 + A2 + B, unified by one new
`session-query last-landing` Go query. A1 (branch merged) is git-only; A2 (branch
also reaped) and B (rewrite/descendant gate) both need the landing SHA, so they
share the query. B was weighed against E-1417's in-flight after-conflict diagnosis:
kept because it upgrades the amend case from a guessed candidate (after a confusing
conflict) to a precise refusal BEFORE the rebase. E-1417 stays the safety net for
source conflicts B can't predetermine. Both edit land_worktree — rebase E-1308 onto
E-1417 and share the reset+reapply wording.

---

Added case (Claude session, 2026-07-09; now folded into the plan as Facet B):

The `git branch --merged main` test catches only FULLY-merged branches. It misses
the re-land failure where a branch's commit was `git commit --amend`-ed AFTER its
content had already been landed: the branch is a partial duplicate of main plus a
new delta — not fully merged — so `--merged` is false and land proceeds into a
source-file rebase conflict.

Gate (reuses task_landings, which records each landing's SHA): on a re-land (task
has >=1 task_landings row), require the branch HEAD to be a descendant of the last
landed SHA — `git merge-base --is-ancestor <last_landed_sha> HEAD`. A correct
follow-up (a new commit stacked on a branch first rebased onto main) passes; an
amend/rewrite fails. On failure, refuse BEFORE the rebase and print the reset+reapply
recovery rather than a misleading auto-file message.

Concrete repro: E-1750's first commit was landed; a follow-up was made by amending
that commit instead of stacking a new one; the next `just land` rebase re-applied the
whole change onto a main that already had it -> CONFLICT in
internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status.go. Recovery was manual reset-to-main +
re-apply-delta. Couples to E-1417 (the diagnosis half).

because main contains the landing SHA; only an amend/rewrite of the landed commit is
refused. This makes the amend case a precise PRE-conflict refusal; E-1417 remains the
after-conflict safety net for source conflicts B cannot predetermine.

## Files
- `internal/sessionquerycmd/session_query.go` (+ usage lines in `cmd/endless-go/main.go`)
  — the `last-landing` subcommand.
- `src/endless/worktree_cmd.py` — `_last_landing` helper; Facet A block at the
  `target is None` branch; Facet B gate before Step 4.

## Coordination with E-1417 (in flight, same function)
E-1417 rewrites Step 4's conflict handler; E-1308 adds a pre-Step-4 gate and the
`target is None` branch — adjacent code. Rebase E-1308 onto E-1417 (or sequence after
it). Keep B's refusal message and E-1417's already-landed candidate consistent — BOTH
facts-and-hints that defer the destructive fix to the branch owner's judgment, never a
prescribed bare `git reset --hard` (a lander who didn't author the branch could lose
work). No behavioral clash: B refuses earlier, so E-1417's Step-4 handler is simply
not reached for the rewrite case.

## Tests
- Go (`internal/sessionquerycmd`, pattern per its `*_test.go`): `last-landing` returns
  the newest landing's SHA; empty when none.
- Python worktree-land suite (real git repos, pattern per
  `tests/test_worktree_land_orphan_drop.py`):
  - A1: worktree dir removed + branch merged → friendly message, exit 0.
  - A2: worktree + branch gone + a `task_landings` row → friendly message.
  - A3: neither → today's error preserved.
  - B: landed once then branch amended (not a descendant) → refuse before rebase with
    reset+reapply; branch with a new commit stacked (descendant) → proceeds.

## Verify
Deliver `tests/tasks/e-1308-verify.sh`; handoff is exactly:

    esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1308-verify.sh

Exercises A1/A2/A3/B against crafted throwaway git repos plus the `last-landing` Go
query, per the model of `tests/tasks/e-1577-verify.sh`.

## Non-goals
- Auto-recovering the rewrite (Facet B refuses + instructs; it does not reset for the
  user — land stays non-interactive).
- Changing the reaper or the landing-record flow.
- Replacing E-1417's after-conflict diagnosis (kept as the safety net).

fields.analysis:
Scope decision (with Mike, 2026-07-11): FULL — A1 + A2 + B, unified by one new
`session-query last-landing` Go query. A1 (branch merged) is git-only; A2 (branch
also reaped) and B (rewrite/descendant gate) both need the landing SHA, so they
share the query. B was weighed against E-1417's in-flight after-conflict diagnosis:
kept because it upgrades the amend case from a guessed candidate (after a confusing
conflict) to a precise refusal BEFORE the rebase. E-1417 stays the safety net for
source conflicts B can't predetermine. Both edit land_worktree — rebase E-1308 onto
E-1417 and keep the recovery wording consistent.

Recovery framing (Mike, 2026-07-11): Facet B's refusal must NOT prescribe a bare
`git reset --hard` + reapply. Whoever runs `land` may not be the session that
authored the branch, so a blanket destructive command risks losing commits. Report
facts (HEAD not a descendant of the landing at <sha>) + inspection hints, and defer
the fix to the branch owner's judgment; mention reset+reapply only as a possible
judgment call. Same principle applies to E-1417's already-landed candidate.

---

Added case (Claude session, 2026-07-09; now folded into the plan as Facet B):

The `git branch --merged main` test catches only FULLY-merged branches. It misses
the re-land failure where a branch's commit was `git commit --amend`-ed AFTER its
content had already been landed: the branch is a partial duplicate of main plus a
new delta — not fully merged — so `--merged` is false and land proceeds into a
source-file rebase conflict.

Gate (reuses task_landings, which records each landing's SHA): on a re-land (task
has >=1 task_landings row), require the branch HEAD to be a descendant of the last
landed SHA — `git merge-base --is-ancestor <last_landed_sha> HEAD`. A correct
follow-up (a new commit stacked on a branch first rebased onto main) passes; an
amend/rewrite fails. On failure, refuse BEFORE the rebase and print the reset+reapply
recovery rather than a misleading auto-file message.

Concrete repro: E-1750's first commit was landed; a follow-up was made by amending
that commit instead of stacking a new one; the next `just land` rebase re-applied the
whole change onto a main that already had it -> CONFLICT in
internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status.go. Recovery was manual reset-to-main +
re-apply-delta. Couples to E-1417 (the diagnosis half).

fields.text:
# `endless task report <id>` — steering-prompt reporting command

Delivered design (revised from the original `--xml` spec during co-design with
Mike; supersedes the earlier `--text`). Rationale for the reframe lives in the
E-1760 outcome and this task's analysis; ED-1531 was updated to match.

## What it is

End-of-session reports stop being freeform prose the agent composes. The agent
runs `endless task report <id>`; the command computes the facts it can, gates
the one free-text escape hatch, and prints a **steering prompt** that tells the
agent to relay only those facts to the user — plainly, no ceremony.

The original single `--xml` document conflated three concerns; splitting them
collapsed the design:

1. **stdout is a steering prompt** (plain text), not a verbatim relay and not
   data. It hands the agent the relevant facts and steers a terse report.
2. **No intermediate XML.** Facts are read from git/DB into a struct; the
   agent's non-computable input is a small JSON payload. Nothing serializes to
   XML — the `--xml` surface the title named is retired.
3. **No persistence here.** Capturing the facts as queryable rows is E-1777.

## Command

```
endless task report <id> [--json '<payload>' | --json-file <path>]
```

Positional `<id>`; status-agnostic (does not change status). Normal path is no
payload at all → zero free-text entries → zero Haiku calls.

Payload (all optional):
```json
{
  "notes":     [{"kind": "anomaly|discovery", "text": "…"}],
  "questions": [{"text": "…", "type": "text|integer|real|boolean|choice", "style": "…"}]
}
```
Malformed JSON / unknown key / out-of-set kind|type → rejected (ClickException).

## Computed facts (steering prompt only; not persisted)

- **status**, **landed**, **successors** (tasks this task `blocks` + tasks that
  `cleans_up` it, each with status), **children** — one Go read via
  `session-query task-report --id N` (`internal/monitor/task_report.go`,
  `internal/sessionquerycmd`). No Python DB read (house rule).
- **git/worktree anomalies** — reuse the existing DB-free `worktree-anomalies`
  probe. Surfaced to the AGENT, with prompt guidance to mention to the user only
  when unexpected. Not persisted, not analytic.

Empty categories are omitted from the prompt (terse for the human).

Dropped vs. the original schema: `<verify>` (stop-gap pending E-1596's
verify.toml), `<deliverable present>` (redundant with `tasks.outcome`),
`commit ahead` (derivable, low snapshot value).

## Per-entry Haiku gate

Fires only when a payload entry exists. Reuses the hook-suppressed
`internal_claude.run_internal_claude(model="haiku")`. Notes get the note-check
("real non-computable fact, or absence of a problem?"); questions get the
question-check ("real decision, or restating settled state?"). A bounced entry
raises with agent-aware anti-rationalization phrasing. Model is FIXED (Haiku),
not a knob. **Fail-open** on Haiku unavailability — a handoff must always be
completable; the gate is a best-effort quality filter (diverges from the
verb-gate's fail-closed because a false block is far costlier here).

## Tunable wording (user lever)

The steer prompt and the two check prompts live in a user-editable JSONL file
(`report_prompts.py`), precedence project `.endless/report-prompts.jsonl` →
machine `~/.config/endless/report-prompts.jsonl` → embedded default (verbs.jsonl
precedent). Records `{"name":"steer|note-check|question-check","text":"…"}`.

## Files

- `internal/monitor/task_report.go` (+ test) — computed facts core.
- `internal/sessionquerycmd/session_query.go` (+ task_report_test.go) — the
  `task-report` JSON subcommand.
- `src/endless/report_cmd.py` — parse, gate, compute, render.
- `src/endless/report_prompts.py` — tunable config surface.
- `src/endless/cli.py` — the `task report` command.
- `tests/test_task_report.py`, `tests/tasks/e-1771-verify.sh`.

## Verify

`esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1771-verify.sh`

payload.title: task report emits a steering prompt, not a verbatim relay, and carries no intermediate XML
payload.description: Revises ED-1531 after E-1771 co-design. Two specifics changed: (1) task report prints a STEERING PROMPT that hands the agent the computed facts and instructs a terse ceremony-free report, rather than output the agent echoes verbatim; (2) NO intermediate XML — input is a small JSON payload (notes/questions only), computed facts are read from git/DB into a struct, stdout is the prompt; the --xml surface is retired. Unchanged: the tool produces all computable facts (agent never types them); the sole free-text hatch is guarded by a scoped, tunable, fixed-model Haiku check; interception is a CLI command not a hook. Persisting facts as queryable rows is deferred to E-1777.

fields.analysis:
# Agreed data model (from E-1771 co-design)

Design input for this task's schema brainstorm, settled while building E-1771.
E-1771 computes these facts and renders them into a steering prompt but does NOT
persist; this task writes them as queryable rows.

## Proposed tables

```
report            (id, task_id FK, session_id, status, created_at)
report_task_ref   (report_id FK, task_id FK, role[successor|child], relation?, status_at_report)
report_note       (report_id FK, kind[anomaly|discovery], text, gate_verdict)
report_question   (report_id FK, text, answer?, type[text|integer|real|boolean|choice], style?, gate_verdict)
```

- Related tasks are an **FK to `tasks`**, not duplicated detail. Snapshot only
  the fields whose historical value you'd query — **status_at_report** (and
  likely **phase**) — and live-join the stable detail (title, type, relations).
- **Never capture transient render/dirty state.** Git/worktree anomalies are an
  agent concern surfaced in the prompt; they are neither user-facing nor
  analytic, so they get no table (decided in E-1771).
- Questions: `type` is the data type; `style` is a presentation hint
  (`yes-no`/`true-false` for boolean, `single`/`multiple` for choice) — kept
  distinct because a true/false question is not necessarily yes/no.
- Explicit-about-absence applies HERE (an empty successor set is a recorded
  fact), unlike the steering prompt which stays silent on empty categories.

## Out of scope here (per E-1774)
- `<tests>` from CTRF — rides with this capture work when added.
- Regression-diffing against last-green baseline — separate task, needs this
  captured history first.

## Element/attribute source
The XML sketch that shaped this (element vs attribute rule: scalars are
attributes, collections are child elements) maps 1:1 onto these tables. No
intermediate XML serialization is needed — E-1771 reads into a struct, this task
writes the struct to rows.

fields.title: Add a task report command that steers agent handoffs to just the facts

fields.text:
# FULL STATUS bypass keyword + mid-session reporting guidance

## Mechanism (decided)
Both pieces live in the **handoff templates** — the same surface E-1759 rewrote,
NOT the `task report` output template. Specifically the shared partial
`internal/templatecmd/templates/handoff/_close.tmpl` (`{{define "handoff_close"}}`),
which all six per-type handoff templates pull in via `{{template "handoff_close" .}}`.

Two additions to the reporting discipline already in that partial:
1. **Route reporting through `endless task report`** — state, as the default,
   that end-of-session and status reporting are produced by feeding the
   structured payload to `endless task report <id> --xml` and relaying its
   output verbatim, not composed as freeform prose. (This is the line that
   references E-1771's command — see Blocked-by.)
2. **`FULL STATUS` bypass keyword** — when the user types `FULL STATUS`, the
   agent answers UNCONSTRAINED for that one response (per-response, not a sticky
   mode). This is the explicit "elaborate when I ASK" lever.

## Scope
**Spawned sessions only** for now — the handoff templates reach only sessions
started via `endless task spawn`. Extending the discipline (and `FULL STATUS`)
to non-spawned sessions would mean the all-sessions SessionStart injection
(`FormatTasks` in `internal/monitor/task.go`), which currently carries only task
facts. Deferred: revisit only if ceremony proves a problem in non-spawned
sessions.

## Tunability (free)
Handoff templates honor `.local.tmpl` → `.tmpl` → embedded precedence, so
`FULL STATUS` and the reporting posture become per-project overridable without
touching product source — the "user lever" principle from ED-1531 at no extra
cost.

## Blocked-by E-1771
The routing default (#1) references `endless task report`, which E-1771 builds.
Landing that line before the command exists would point live spawn prompts at a
missing command. The `FULL STATUS` half (#2) is independent, but the task is
gated as a unit so the template lands coherent once the command exists.

## Verification
Per-task script `tests/tasks/e-1773-verify.sh` (model: existing
`tests/tasks/e-1577-*`). The deterministic surface is the *rendered* handoff
output, so the script renders the handoff templates and asserts content:

1. For each handoff type (`endless-go template render handoff/<type>.md` with
   sample render data — foreground and `.bg` variants), assert the output now
   contains:
   - the `FULL STATUS` bypass instruction, and
   - the "route reporting through `endless task report`" default.
2. Assert the pre-existing discipline is intact — the `endless worktree check`
   line, the "do not confirm the negative" clause, and the return line
   (foreground) / background stop instruction (`.bg`) — so the additions did not
   displace what E-1759 established.

The behavioral half (an agent actually answering unconstrained on `FULL STATUS`)
is guidance, not script-testable; it is exercised in use, not asserted here.

Handoff verify line: `esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1773-verify.sh`.

# E-1308 — Detect already-landed situations in `worktree land` and message accordingly

## Context

`endless worktree land E-NNN` mishandles three "the work already landed" situations
by treating them as failures:

- The worktree was removed by a prior land → `_branch_for_task` returns `None` and
  land raises `"No endless-managed worktree for E-NNN"` (`worktree_cmd.py:1628-1632`),
  implying the work is lost. It isn't — it's in main.
- The branch was rewritten relative to a landing that already happened (e.g. a
  `git commit --amend` of an already-landed commit) → land proceeds straight into a
  confusing Step-4 rebase conflict. Observed repro: the E-1750 land amended a
  landed commit; the re-land conflicted in `session_status.go`.

Full scope decided with Mike 2026-07-11: cover all three via one shared last-landing
lookup — A1 (branch merged), A2 (branch also reaped), B (branch is a rewrite).

## 1. New capability — read a task's last landing (Go)

No Go query returns a task's landing SHA today (`session-query` has none; the Python
`landed_item` path reads `task_landings` via SQLite, which new code must not extend —
E-1486). Add subcommand **`session-query last-landing --id <task-id>`** in
`internal/sessionquerycmd/session_query.go` (dispatched from the `session-query` case
in `cmd/endless-go/main.go`; update the usage lines at `main.go:14` and `:195`).

Query (main DB):

    SELECT merge_commit_sha, branch, landed_at
      FROM task_landings WHERE task_id = ?
     ORDER BY landed_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT 1

Output: JSON `{"merge_commit_sha","branch","landed_at"}`; empty output when the task
has no landing (mirror the empty-handling of the existing subcommands, e.g.
`task-text`). Python wraps it as `_last_landing(task_id) -> dict | None` via
`shutil.which("endless-go")` + `config.go_db_context_args()` (land already pins main
through `default_db_to_main`), returning `None` when there is no landing.

## 2. Facet A — worktree already gone (`land_worktree`, the `target is None` branch ~L1632)

Before raising "No endless-managed worktree", in order:

- **A1 (git-only):** a branch matching `task/<NNN>-*` exists AND is listed by
  `git branch --merged <base>` → print
  `"E-<NNN> already landed (<branch-tip-short-sha>); its worktree was removed by an
  earlier land. Nothing to do."` and RETURN success (exit 0).
- **A2 (uses §1):** else, if `_last_landing(NNN)` is not None → print
  `"E-<NNN> already landed (<merge_commit_sha-short>); its worktree and branch were
  reaped. Nothing to do."` and RETURN success.
- **A3:** else → today's `"No endless-managed worktree for E-<NNN>"` error (the work
  is genuinely unaccounted for).

The subject task's own `E-<NNN>` may appear (the user typed it); the house-rule ban is
on citing UNRELATED internal task IDs — none here.

## 3. Facet B — branch is a rewrite of already-landed content (pre-rebase gate)

Insert after Step 3.8's dirty guard (`_guard_dirty_worktree`, ~L1741) and BEFORE
Step 4's `git rebase base_branch` (~L1743):

- `land = _last_landing(NNN)`; if `None` → skip (first land — normal).
- Else if `git -C <wt> merge-base --is-ancestor <land.merge_commit_sha> HEAD` exits
  non-zero → HEAD is NOT a descendant of the landing → the branch was rewritten
  relative to it (e.g. an amended already-landed commit). **Refuse before the rebase
  mutates anything:** `raise click.ClickException(msg)`. Because the descendant check
  is DEFINITIVE (unlike E-1417's Step-4 handler, which guesses among causes), `msg`
  names the cause confidently: HEAD is not a descendant of the branch's recorded
  landing at `<sha>`, so land is refusing to avoid duplicating already-landed work.
  It then presents the SAME already-landed recovery E-1417 ships — the shared
  `_already_landed_recovery(wt, base)` snippet (delta captured to a patch FIRST, then
  reset + re-apply), so the sequence never loses the branch's new work even when the
  runner didn't author it — plus a one-line note to confirm branch ownership / that
  the captured delta is the intended change before running it, and inspection hints
  (`git -C <wt> log <base>..HEAD`, `git -C <wt> diff <base>...HEAD`). No emojis, no
  unrelated internal IDs.
- Else (descendant, or no landing) → proceed to Step 4 unchanged.

A correct follow-up (a new commit on a branch first rebased onto main) passes,
because main contains the landing SHA; only an amend/rewrite of the landed commit is
refused. This makes the amend case a precise PRE-conflict refusal; E-1417 remains the
after-conflict safety net for source conflicts B cannot predetermine.

## Files
- `internal/sessionquerycmd/session_query.go` (+ usage lines in `cmd/endless-go/main.go`)
  — the `last-landing` subcommand.
- `src/endless/worktree_cmd.py` — `_last_landing` helper; Facet A block at the
  `target is None` branch; Facet B gate before Step 4; extract
  `_already_landed_recovery(wt, base)` from the shipped `_rebase_conflict_message`
  candidate 2 and call it from both that function and Facet B (keeps the wording
  identical; a pure refactor of E-1417's landed code, behavior unchanged).

## Coordination with E-1417 (LANDED — commit b1efcc28)
E-1417 already shipped `_rebase_conflict_message` in `worktree_cmd.py`. Its
source-conflict "candidate 2" is the already-landed recovery and is SAFE by
construction — it captures the branch's delta to a patch BEFORE resetting:

    git -C <wt> diff <base>...HEAD > /tmp/land-delta.patch
    git -C <wt> reset --hard <base>
    git -C <wt> apply /tmp/land-delta.patch
    git -C <wt> commit -am "<describe your change>"

E-1308 branches from current main (which has E-1417) — no rebase-onto-in-flight.
To keep B's refusal and E-1417's candidate byte-identical, EXTRACT that recovery
block into a small shared builder (e.g. `_already_landed_recovery(wt, base) -> str`)
and call it from BOTH `_rebase_conflict_message`'s candidate 2 and Facet B's message.
`_rebase_conflict_message` itself is only reachable mid-conflict (it reads
REBASE_HEAD / unmerged paths), so B cannot call it directly — B builds its own
message from the shared recovery snippet plus the definitive cause line. No
behavioral clash: B refuses earlier, so E-1417's Step-4 handler is simply not reached
for the rewrite case.

## Tests
- Go (`internal/sessionquerycmd`, pattern per its `*_test.go`): `last-landing` returns
  the newest landing's SHA; empty when none.
- Python worktree-land suite (real git repos, pattern per
  `tests/test_worktree_land_orphan_drop.py`):
  - A1: worktree dir removed + branch merged → friendly message, exit 0.
  - A2: worktree + branch gone + a `task_landings` row → friendly message.
  - A3: neither → today's error preserved.
  - B: landed once then branch amended (not a descendant) → refuse before rebase with
    reset+reapply; branch with a new commit stacked (descendant) → proceeds.

## Verify
Deliver `tests/tasks/e-1308-verify.sh`; handoff is exactly:

    esu && ./tests/tasks/e-1308-verify.sh

Exercises A1/A2/A3/B against crafted throwaway git repos plus the `last-landing` Go
query, per the model of `tests/tasks/e-1577-verify.sh`.

## Non-goals
- Auto-recovering the rewrite (Facet B refuses + instructs; it does not reset for the
  user — land stays non-interactive).
- Changing the reaper or the landing-record flow.
- Replacing E-1417's after-conflict diagnosis (kept as the safety net).

share the query. B was weighed against E-1417's in-flight after-conflict diagnosis:

Dependency check found no consumers: the only non-test references are its own module and CLI registration; worktree_cmd.py mentions are an unrelated commit-message string, the Go 'activity' hits are last_activity idle-throttling, and event_bridge.py:98 is only a comment noting actor.session_id enables activity filtering (session_id on events has independent uses and stays). payload.title: The endless guide is agent-first; user-only commands live in an appendix, not inlined in agent sections
payload.description: The endless guide's sections are written for the AI agent, so context/token load is minimized. Commands intended only for human users (interactive tmux navigation, live-watch views, etc.) are documented in a separate appendix (docs/guide/appendix-a.md, 'User-focused commands') and referenced from agent-facing sections with a single minimal pointer — never inlined. The appendix may appear in the section list, but naming it an 'appendix' signals agents to deprioritize it; they pull it into context only to inform a user. No guide/guide_map code change is needed.

fields.text:
# E-1780 — Document the session commands: agent-facing in sessions.md, user-facing in a new appendix

## Context

`docs/guide/sessions.md` covers status snapshots, "who am I" discovery, and the DB
internals of the status subsystem, but none of the navigation / observation /
inspection command family that has since grown on the `session` group. The guide-map
prepends "▸ AGENT — read this: `endless guide sessions`" to every `session`
subcommand, so that pointer currently resolves to a section that never explains the
commands. This task makes it honest — and applies the guide-audience convention we just
recorded.

## Convention this applies (ED-1533)

The endless guide is **agent-first**: sections are written for the AI agent to minimize
context load. Commands intended only for human users are documented in a separate
**appendix**, referenced from agent-facing sections with a single minimal pointer —
never inlined. The appendix may appear in the section list; naming it an "appendix"
signals agents to deprioritize it (they pull it in only to inform a user). No
`guide`/`guide_map` code change is needed to realize this.

## Command classification (settled with Mike)

- **Agent-facing → stay in `sessions.md`:** `status` (cheap self-orientation), `show`
  and `list` (an agent coordinating inspects sibling/child sessions), plus the existing

fields.description: Make end-of-session reporting structured and ceremony-free: the agent runs 'endless task report <id>', which computes the facts it can (status, follow-ups, children, worktree state), gates the one free-text escape hatch (notes/questions) with a per-entry Haiku check, and prints a steering prompt that steers the agent to relay only those facts to the user, plainly, no ceremony. Input is a small JSON payload (notes/questions only); stdout is a steering prompt (not a verbatim relay); no intermediate XML. Check wording lives in a user-editable config surface; the Haiku model is fixed. Persisting reports as queryable rows is E-1777. Full spec in --text; rationale in E-1760 outcome and ED-1531/ED-1532.

Capture the objective facts of each end-of-session report as structured, queryable DB rows — the session_tasks -> session status trajectory, where a table that began as 'tasks a session mentioned' became the backbone of critical tooling. Split out of E-1771 (which stays the lean ceremony-killing report command) so the report command need not also design persistence. Store normalized relational rows (a report row plus child rows: notes, questions, task refs), NOT one opaque blob, so tooling can query individual facts. Decide the table shape, what to capture, and how tooling queries it. Precondition for regression-diffing (E-1778).
fields.analysis:
# Agreed data model (from E-1771 co-design)

Design input for this task's schema, settled while building E-1771. E-1771
computes these facts and renders them into a steering prompt but does NOT
persist; this task writes them as queryable rows.

## Proposed tables

```
report            (id, task_id FK, session_id, status, created_at)
report_task_ref   (report_id FK, task_id FK, role[successor|child], relation?, status_at_report)
report_note       (report_id FK, kind[anomaly|discovery], text, gate_verdict)
report_question   (report_id FK, text, answer?, type[text|integer|real|boolean|choice], style?, gate_verdict)
```

- Related tasks are an **FK to `tasks`**, not duplicated detail. Snapshot only
  the fields whose historical value you'd query — **status_at_report** (and
  likely **phase**) — and live-join the stable detail (title, type, relations).
- **Never capture transient render/dirty state.** Git/worktree anomalies are an
  agent concern surfaced in the prompt; they are neither user-facing nor
  analytic, so they get no table (decided in E-1771).
- Questions: `type` is the data type; `style` is a presentation hint
  (`yes-no`/`true-false` for boolean, `single`/`multiple` for choice) — kept
  distinct because a true/false question is not necessarily yes/no.
- Explicit-about-absence applies HERE (an empty successor set is a recorded
  fact), unlike the steering prompt which stays silent on empty categories.
- Store **normalized relational rows**, never one opaque blob — the whole point
  of capture is that tooling can query individual facts. The scalar-vs-collection
  rule that shaped these tables (scalars are columns, collections are child
  rows) maps 1:1 from the fact struct E-1771 already builds; no serialization
  step is needed — E-1771 reads facts into the struct, this task writes the
  struct to rows.
